items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: so Benny Powell proposed a project we’re going to do soon, called the Trio of Griots.

ctx.x: So now, I found out I wasn’t the only one, that Benny Powell the trombone player does the same thing, well he’s got quite a history too. And Billy Harper, the tenor player. So I guess the three of us were the ones who were doing it most you know, so Benny Powell proposed a project we’re going to do soon, called the Trio of Griots. I think Griot means —

items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: Oh, Benny Powell as a young man, he was talking about being, was it at his uncle’s house

ctx.x: Real briefly, tell him what Benny Powell said about the trombone.

Oh, Benny Powell as a young man, he was talking about being, was it at his uncle’s house, and he just happened to lean back like a kid and there was this trombone sitting back there, and, “What’s that?” And that was the whole start, because he’d been playing drums I guess, the bass drum he said.

Well they tried to teach me the bass drum, once I got into the Army too, to make it look good I mean they had to put down something, you know I had to show I played something else. So one day they got a small nucleus of the band to go out to play you know troops that are finishing Basic Training. On their last day, part of the band will go out and meet them and play for them to march back to the company area, you know to sort of give them the spirit, well it’s over now you know. So they said, “All right, Mance,…
